summary: A solid IELTS listening paper with the right four settings and plenty of real traps. Part 2's matching box and Part 3's MCQs are well paraphrased. Two Part 4 keys accepted words that are never heard on the recording ('aeroplanes', 'antenna'); in IELTS only the heard word counts, so I removed them.
strengths: Part 1 corrections on most gaps: beginners/intermediate, 7th/14th March, Lake/Garden Room, 500/450, 12/10 students, trainers/boots, phone/email.
Part 2 box options are paraphrased, not copied (carries the name of / is named after; twice the size / made bigger; every Saturday / one day a week; caretaker's flat / different purpose).
Part 3 (820 words) is a believable planning discussion; each MCQ names and rejects both distractors, and the multi-select items require following three or four rejected options.
Part 4 notes follow the lecture's order and each gap is one concrete noun.

issues.problem: Key also accepted 'aeroplanes', which the lecturer never says (he says 'the first aircraft'). IELTS gap answers must be words heard.
Key also accepted 'antenna', which is not heard (the lecturer says 'aerial').
Pair's question side 'early aircraft' contained the answer, which the student does not see in the notes.
issues.change: Pair now ['influenced the builders of the first', 'his design influenced early'].

issues.problem: Most Part 1 rows repeat the receptionist's wording (top floor, printing materials, tripods are provided, spare battery), so Questions 2-5, 7 and 9 have no paraphrase.
issues.change: Normal for Part 1; no change needed.

issues.problem: Part 4 notes 33, 35 and 39 keep the lecture's phrases ('frighten away', 'metal ... tied to the line', 'standing on a').
issues.change: Reword in a future edit, e.g. 33 'to scare off ______ that ate young crops'.
